sections.h2: Which Erie County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Two county offices matter most to a homeowner: the Assessment Office, which sets the value your tax bill is built on, and the Revenue and Tax Claim Bureau, which collects delinquent taxes. Both work out of Erie County Courthouse, 140 West Sixth Street, Erie, PA 16501. Appeals go to Room 104, and delinquent taxes are paid in Room 110.

The Assessment Office describes its job as assessing all real estate in the county accurately and uniformly while running the various tax programs. The Tax Claim Bureau is one of four divisions of the county Department of Finance. It collects delinquent taxes for the county, for the City of Erie and the other municipalities, and for the school districts, then passes the money out to each of them every month.

Local tax collectors bill current-year taxes. If you need the amount due for the year of a sale, ask the tax collector for your municipality rather than the county.

sections.h2: How do you appeal an Erie County assessment?
sections.html:
File a Notice of Intention to Appeal Property Assessment with the Erie County Board of Appeals, and make sure it arrives between January 1 and August 1. The county's form says appeals are heard from July through October.

  • Use one form for each parcel.
  • Include the county parcel ID, the property location, your own estimate of value and the reason for the appeal.
  • List up to three comparable properties that sold recently or are listed for sale, by county index number, name and address.
  • Pay the non-refundable filing fee with a check made out to County of Erie.

The filing fee is $50.00 for the main parcel, plus $10.00 for each extra parcel that makes up the property as a whole, set by County Council Ordinance No. 157 of 2007. The form warns that comparable assessments are not treated as an indication of fair market value, and an exterior photograph of the property is available at the hearing.

Filing opens your property to revaluation, so the assessment may go down, go up or stay where it is. Think about that risk before you file on a property you plan to sell soon. If a corporation owns the house, the form must be signed by an officer. The county also lists a Catastrophic Loss Appeal form for damage cases.

sections.h2: What exemption and program forms does Erie County offer?
sections.html:
The Assessment Office's Documents and Forms page lists a set of applications that change who is taxed or how much. Some matter to a seller, because a change of owner should be recorded with the county once the deed is done.

  • Application for Homestead and Farmstead Exclusions
  • Application for Exemption From Erie County Real Property Taxes
  • Owner Change Form and Owner Registry Form
  • Clean and Green application, Clean and Green information and the Act 319 Notice of Conveyance
  • Mobile Home Change of Ownership Form
  • Change of Address form

Clean and Green land has its own notice when it is conveyed, so a buyer of a farm parcel should look at that form before closing. The page also posts millage rate charts for every year back to 2011, with a revised chart for 2026. Millage rates differ by municipality and school district, so use the chart that matches the house.

sections.h2: When is the Erie County tax sale?
sections.html:
The 2026 upset sale was set for Monday, September 28, 2026 at 9:00 a.m., held online through GovEase. An upset sale offers parcels whose taxes are at least two years delinquent.

Bidders pay a $60.00 non-refundable registration fee. The minimum bid is about the sum of the delinquent and current taxes plus municipal liens, with a $25 deed preparation fee and a $100 engineering fee on City of Erie properties. A property that does not sell can move to the judicial sale, which is run by a law firm, and the owner of that property may not bid on it.

sections.h2: Can you stop a sale or pay delinquent taxes in Erie County?
sections.html:
Yes. Even after a bid is made at the upset sale, the owner can pay the delinquency before the winning bidder pays the upset price, and the property is treated as if it had never been offered. Once the bidder pays in full by 3:30 p.m. on sale day, there is no redemption period.

Delinquent taxes are paid in Room 110 of the courthouse, Monday through Friday from 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, and the office is closed on county holidays. It takes cash, attorney IOLTA checks, money orders, certified checks, business or personal checks and MasterCard or Visa. Online payments carry an extra fee of usually around 3%. Ask the Bureau for a current figure at 814-451-6206 because interest and costs are added from time to time.

A stay of sale agreement works as an installment plan, but it cannot be made online.

  • An owner named on the deed must appear in person with state-issued ID or a passport.
  • The down payment is at least 25% of the most recent two years of delinquent taxes.
  • Any older unpaid taxes must be paid in full.
  • A default bars a new installment agreement for three years.

sections.h2: Can you sell a house in Erie County with property tax still due?
sections.html:
You can, as long as the delinquent balance is paid out of the sale proceeds or before closing. Ask the Tax Claim Bureau for a payoff figure close to the closing date, since interest and costs keep being added, and ask your municipality's tax collector for the amount on the current year's bill.

A house already in the sale process is harder. The owner of a property headed to the judicial or repository sale cannot bid on it, and repository sales carry no right of redemption. If your house is on a published list, talk to the Bureau about a stay of sale before you sign a contract, because that may buy time for a closing.

Title work matters just as much to the buyer. Liens, judgments and rents of record follow a property, which is why tax sale bidders are told to order a title search. A buyer's title agent will do the same on an ordinary sale and will insist on payoff of anything found.

sections.h2: What do Erie County housing numbers look like?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures put the median value of owner-occupied homes in Erie County at $177,000, with 68.1% of homes owner-occupied. There were 110,587 households. Median household income was $63,354, and 14.7% of residents were below the poverty line.

Owners with a mortgage had median monthly costs of $1,393, and those without a mortgage $572, while median gross rent was $904. The county issued 243 building permits in 2025.

faqs.q: When can I file an assessment appeal in Erie County?
faqs.a: Appeal forms are accepted from January 1 through August 1. The county form also says hearings run from July through October.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to appeal an Erie County assessment?
faqs.a: The non-refundable filing fee is $50.00 for the main parcel plus $10.00 for each additional parcel that makes up the property. Checks are made out to County of Erie.

faqs.q: Where do I pay delinquent property taxes in Erie County?
faqs.a: Pay in Room 110 of the Erie County Courthouse, 140 West Sixth Street, Monday through Friday from 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM. You can also pay online from the parcel's tax page, with an added fee of usually around 3%.

faqs.q: What is a stay of sale agreement in Erie County?
faqs.a: It is an installment plan that keeps a delinquent property out of a tax sale. It needs at least 25% of the last two years of delinquent taxes down, payment of all older taxes, and an owner on the deed appearing in person with photo ID.

faqs.q: Can the owner buy back a house after an Erie County upset sale?
faqs.a: Not after the sale is complete. The owner can pay the delinquency before the winning bidder pays the upset price, but once the bidder pays in full by 3:30 p.m. on sale day there is no period of redemption.
